refsect1.title: DESCRIPTION
refsect1.para: The ringbuffer command is an ensemble of commands that manipulate NSCL ring buffers. A command ensemble is a single command that has subcommands. The subcommands determine what is actually done. See ENSEMBLE COMMANDS for a description of each ensemble subcommand.

listitem.para: Creates a new ring buffer. The name parameter is mandatory and is the name of the new ring buffer. The ringbuffer name must not have any / characters embedded in it. Since the ringbuffer command is actually a Tcl script it's probably a good idea to avoid characters that have special meaning to Tcl as well.

If the environment variable NSCLDAQ_DEFAULT_RINGMBYTES is defined and can be decoded as an integer, the value sets the default megabytes of ring buffer data size. --datasize can be used to explicitly set the data size.

Formats the header of the ring buffer name. name must already exist. If provided, the value of the optional option --maxconsumers determines how many consumers can simultaneously connect to the ring buffer.

Marks the ring buffer name for deletion. name immediately is no longer available for new attachments. Once all existing attached clients have detached, the ring buffer shared memory region will be deleted.

Outputs the status of all active ring buffers that match pattern to stdout. If pattern is not supplied, it defaults to * which matches the names of all ring buffers. Note that if you use patterns with wildcards you should quote the pattern to suppress the command shell's attempts to do file name expansions. Note that a ring buffer is active if it has attached clients.
If the --host option is supplied, its value is the name of the system whose ring buffers are inquired. This defaults to localhost.

When either --host is not supplied or its value is localhost, the --all and --user options can filter the set of rings that will be present in the output table. By defafult, only rings the user 'owns' will be shown. Note that proxy rings are normally owned by root and therefore won't be shown by default.

If the --all switch is supplied, or --host is not localhost, all rings will be listed. Remote ring lists cannot be filtered at this time because filtering is performed by observing the owner of the shared memory special file and that cannot be done simply for remote rings. In the future, extensions to the ring master protocol may support this filtering.

If supplied, the value of --user must be a comma separated list of usernames. Only rings whose owners are in that list will be displayed. If both --user and --all are explicitly specified, an error is signalled.

Note that since proxy rings are owned by root, it is not possible to restrict the listing to the set of proxy rings that are associated with specific users. The command below, therefore lists all rings owned by the current user and all proxy rings:
The ring buffer status is listed in tabular form. Here is some sample output:
The Name column gives the name of a ring buffer. The remaining line provides information about the ring buffer and any consumer it may have. Subsequent lines provide information about consumers.

Information provided about the ring buffer includes data-size(k) the size of the data area in kilobytes. free the number of kilobytes the producer can put without blocking. max_consumers the maximum number of consumers that can connect to the ring. producer the PID of the producer process, which is -1 if there is no producer. maxget(K) the amount of data available for the consumer that is furthest behind in consuming data in kilobytes. minget the amount of data avilable to the consumer that is most caught up in kilobytes.
Subsequent lines of the table provide the process id of a client and the numuber of kilobytes of un-consumed data for the client (clientdata(k)) in kilobytes.

Lists the names of the active ringbuffers one per line to stdout. By default the ring buffers active in localhost are listed. Using the --host option allows you to specify a different host. Active ring buffers are only those that have clients attached.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Python access to low level ringbuffer operations

refsynopsisdiv.programlisting:
import nscldaq.RingBuffer
RingBuffer.create(ring_name[, databytes=numbytes][, maxconsumers=maxnum]) RingBuffer.remove(ring_name) RingBuffer.format(ring_name[, maxconsumers=maxnum]) if RingBuffer.exists(ring_name): # do something because ring_name is a ringbuffer.
ring_name = RingBuffer.default_name()

refsect1.title: DESCRIPTION
refsect1.para: To use this module, you must have set up an NSCLDAQ version 12.2-009 or higher. The daqsetup.bash script for that version will set up a PYTHONPATH environment variable which supports the import of the nscldaq.RingBuffer module.
The module supports unbound ringbuffer primitives. See METHODS below for information about the operations that are supported.

listitem.para: Attempts to create a new ringbuffer. The name of the new ring buffer will be ring_name. The optional keyword parameter databytes sets the maximum size of the ringbuffer. This defaults to 8Mbytes if not provided. The optional keyword parameter maxconsumers places a limit on the number of consumers that will be allowed to get data from the ringbuffer. This defaults to 100 if not provided.
If the ringbuffer cannot be created a RunTimeError is exception is raised.

Attempts to delete the ringbuffer named ring_name note that the ring master will attempt to kill processes connected to the ring (both the producer and any consumers). If the removal of the ringbuffer fails, a RunTimeError exception will be raised.

Reformats the header of a ring buffer. This should be reserved for cases when you believe the ringbuffer is corrupt. In that case, all clients should be shutdown, rendering the ringbuffer idle. ring_name is the name of the ringbuffer to reformat. The optional maxconsumers sets the maximum number of consumers that can take data from the ring. It is normally safer to remove and then create the ring again.
Returns True if the ringbuffer ring_name exists or False if not.
Returns the default ringbuffer name for the consumer. This is the name of the ringbuffer that e.g. readout frameworks will create if no ringbuffer name is specified on their command line.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Interact with the ring master server

refsynopsisdiv.programlisting:
import nscldaq.RingMaster
port_num = RingMaster.getPort(host[, port=30000]) info = RingMaster.usage([host='localhost'] [, portman=30000])

refsect1.title: DESCRIPTION
refsect1.para: The RingMaster module provies methods to access the NSCLDAQ ringmaster process. The ringmaster process is responsible for managing access to ringbuffers and publishing data about them. To use this module, you must set up a version of NSCLDAQ 12.2-009 or greater. The daqsetup.bash script will define a PYTHONPATH environment vairiable that allows the module to be imported.

listitem.para: Returns the port number on which the ring muster running in the system host is listening on for connections. The optional port is the port on which the FRIB/NSCLDAQ port manager is listening for connections. Normally the default value of 30000 is correct.

Returns information about the ringbuffers and their instantaneous statistics. The host is the host in which this information will be returned. Note that this defaults to localhost returning information about the ringbuffers in the system running the script. The optional parameter portman is the port on which the portmanager in host is listening for connections. It defaults to 30000 which is normally correct.

The information is returned as a, possibly empty, iterable container. Each element of the container is a dict that has the following keys:
name
Name of the ring buffer being described by this dict.
size
Size of the ringbuffer in bytes.
free
Number of free bytes in the ring buffer.
maxconsumers
Maximum number of consumer processes that can get data from this ringbuffer.
producer
The process id of the producer of data into the ring. If there is no producer the value of this key will be -1
maxget
The largest number of bytes a single consumer might be able to get. You can think of this as the data backlog for the consumer that is most behind.
minget
Think of this as the data backlog for the consumer that is most caught up.
consumers
The value of this key is a, possibly empty, array of dicts, one dict per consumer attached to the ring. The dict has two keys: pid; the process id of the consumer, and backlog; the number of bytes of backlog by that consumer.
